record.paper_title: Multi-Head Finite Automata: Characterizations, Concepts and Open Problems
record.original_question: What is the exact state complexity of simulating a nondeterministic two-way one-head finite automaton by a deterministic two-way one-head finite automaton? More precisely, given a 2NFA(1), how many states are sufficient and how many are necessary in the worst case for an equivalent 2DFA(1)?

evidence.quote: Nevertheless, some challenging problems of finite automata are still open. An important example is the question of how many states are sufficient and necessary to simulate 2NFA(1) with 2DFA(1); we refer to [12, 23, 39, 41] for further reading.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A two-way one-head finite automaton over a finite alphabet Σ is a finite-state machine equipped with a read-only input tape (with left and right end-markers) and a single head that may move left, right, or stay, until it accepts or rejects. Such a machine is called a 2DFA(1) if its transition relation is deterministic and a 2NFA(1) if it is nondeterministic. Two automata are equivalent if they accept the same language.

For a 2NFA(1) with n states, let f(n) denote the smallest integer such that every n-state 2NFA(1) admits an equivalent 2DFA(1) with at most f(n) states. Determine f(n) exactly; equivalently, determine matching upper and lower bounds on the number of states sufficient and necessary, in the worst case, to simulate an arbitrary n-state 2NFA(1) by an equivalent 2DFA(1). In particular, decide whether f(n) is bounded by a polynomial in n.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of the state-complexity cost of simulating two-way nondeterministic finite automata by two-way deterministic ones is the classical Sakoda–Sipser question (1978). It is widely regarded as a central open problem in automata theory, with known formal connections to the L vs. NL question (Berman–Lingas, Kapoutsis). Only special cases (unary languages, sweeping/oblivious 2DFAs, outer-nondeterministic 2NFAs, etc.) have been resolved; the general question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Two-way finite automaton - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: It is an open problem whether all 2NFAs can be converted to 2DFAs with polynomially many states, i.e. whether there is a polynomial p(n)-state 2DFA for every n-state 2NFA.
status_evidence.claim: The Sakoda–Sipser question on 2NFA-to-2DFA state complexity remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: Size Complexity of Two-Way Finite Automata (Kapoutsis, DLT 2009)
status_evidence.snippet: The Sakoda–Sipser problem... remains open; partial results are known under various restrictions.
status_evidence.claim: Only restricted versions are solved; the general 2NFA(1)-to-2DFA(1) simulation cost is unknown.
